nice_title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management

first_line_treatment.drug_class: ACE inhibitor (if age <55 and not Afro-Caribbean)
first_line_treatment.notes: First-line choice. Monitor renal function and potassium

first_line_treatment.drug_class: Calcium channel blocker (if age ≥55 or Afro-Caribbean)
first_line_treatment.indication: Step 1 for patients aged ≥55 or Afro-Caribbean origin
first_line_treatment.notes: Amlodipine preferred. Avoid in heart failure

second_line_treatment.indication: Step 2: if not controlled on monotherapy

fourth_line_resistant.notes: Beta-blockers not preferred for hypertension alone

contraindicated_drugs.reason: No added benefit, increased renal risk
Risk of heart block and asystole

monitoring: BP: monthly until at target, then 6-12 monthly
Renal function and electrolytes: before ACE-I/ARB, 1-2 weeks after starting, then annually
Cardiovascular risk assessment: QRISK at diagnosis
End-organ damage: check for LVH, retinopathy, proteinuria
